channel.title: Pier & Point · Potrero Power Station Block 12
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Potrero Power Station Block 12 (Potrero Power Station), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Potrero Power Station Block 12: The Power Station's July 2026 request for higher building heights was still shown as upcoming. The Planning Commission heard it in July and approved it unanimously, sending it to the Board of Supervisors; the record now says so.
item.description: The Power Station's July 2026 request for higher building heights was still shown as upcoming. The Planning Commission heard it in July and approved it unanimously, sending it to the Board of Supervisors; the record now says so. Source: https://www.sfchronicle.com/realestate/article/one-s-f-s-biggest-developments-changing-plans-22365461.php; https://sfstandard.com/2026/08/03/jpm-sf-housing-potrero-power-station/.

item.title: Correction · Potrero Power Station Block 12: The record no longer describes Blocks 11 and 12 as a combined life-science campus: the only source pairing them, the project engineer's page, describes about 430,000 sq ft of office, while the Design for Development permits laboratory and life-science uses on Block 12. The expected completion changed from 2028 (a press figure) to 2029, following the October 2020 Phase 1 approval's 2020-2029 schedule and SocketSite's block table (Block 12 vertical 2027-2029), still marked as a 2020 forecast. The Blocks 11 and 12 design review application milestone is now dated February 2021 and no longer described as the source for the bus shelter, the 'first names Block 12' wording was removed, the dead 2019 draft link was replaced with the final February 2020 document, and two source entries' publisher, title and date were corrected.

item.title: Milestone · Potrero Power Station Block 12: Developer proposes a Development Agreement amendment increasing Block 12's permitted height by 23 feet, and giving Block 12 flexibility to become residential instead of commercial; the Planning Commission considered the request that week (Chronicle, July 29, 2026) and approved the amendment unanimously, sending it to the Board of Supervisors (SF Standard, August 3, 2026); no Board action had been read as of October 2026 (~2026)

Source: San Francisco Chronicle (Laura Waxmann), 2026-07-29; The San Francisco Standard, 2026-08-03.

item.title: Expected · Potrero Power Station Block 12: Completion expected: Block 12 is part of Phase 1 (per the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list, Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), whose development schedule runs 2020-2029 under the October 2020 Phase 1 approval; SocketSite's block-by-block table for that program shows Block 12 vertical development 2027-2029 (~2029)

item.title: Planned · Potrero Power Station Block 12: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement covering the adopted Design for Development, whose Land Use Table (Table 3.1.1) lists Block 12 (the Planning Commission had voted 5-0 on January 30, 2020 to recommend approval of the project); the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date. (Block 12 was later named one of Phase 1's six blocks by the October 2020 Phase 1 Development Phase Application -- a construction-phase assignment, not when it first entered the plan.) (Apr 21, 2020)
